samples.summary: `releasePreviewFontLinks()` removes faces without telling any canvas consumer, so a canvas already repainted from a subset face keeps the wrong glyphs/metrics
samples.evidence: Both editors repaint *on font arrival only*: `packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:1063` listens for `document.fonts` `loadingdone` and calls `clearMeasureCache(); markDirty(); render()`, and `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2676` does the same. A subset link injected by a picker row therefore DOES reach the canvas: connecting it fires `loadingdone`, so the slide/doc text for that family is re-measured and repainted with the `&text=` face (a handful of glyphs, per-character fallback for the rest) — which is exactly the failure mode the new comments describe. Removing the link in `releasePreviewFontLinks()` fires no font event and does not clear the module-scoped measure cache, so nothing repaints back: the wrong rendering (and the poisoned `(font,text)→width` cache entries) survives the release until some unrelated edit marks the renderer dirty. The fix addresses the *lifetime* of the face but not the invalidation of what was painted from it. Reachable whenever a deck/doc uses a non-eager family that has no full link yet — slides never calls `ensureFontLink` for the families a deck uses on open (grep shows only pdf-actions, the toolbars and theme-builder call it).

samples.summary: Docs' font-apply path still calls the Font Loading API without awaiting `ensureFontLink`, and `FontRegistry` caches the resulting no-op as `loaded`
samples.evidence: `ensureFont` does `ensureFontLink(family);` (line 350, promise dropped) and immediately `store.fonts?.ensureFont?.(family)` (line 354). `FontRegistry.ensureFont` (packages/docs/src/view/fonts.ts:293-313) then runs `document.fonts.check(spec)` / `await document.fonts.load(spec)` in exactly the window `ensureFontLink`'s new doc comment (font-catalog.ts:156 "AWAIT IT BEFORE `document.fonts.load()`/`check()`") says is unanswerable: the `@font-face` rules have not parsed, so `load()` resolves against nothing and the registry stores `status = 'loaded'` permanently, never re-attempting. Canvas paint does not lazily trigger a CSS face download, so unless some DOM node happens to use the family the face is never fetched and the doc keeps laying out in the fallback. This delta introduced the awaited pattern for the slides caller (`apply-font-family.ts:39`) and for pdf-actions but left this caller on the old unawaited shape — the branch's own lessons doc (docs/tasks/active/20260825-font-preview-subset-lessons.md:97) states the contract is only real once existing callers are read.

samples.summary: The new stylesheet wait is unbounded: a link that neither loads nor errors means the single dirty-gated repaint never happens
samples.evidence: `linked.then(() => document.fonts.load(...)).then(() => { markDirty(); render(); })` only runs if `ensureFontLink`'s promise settles, which depends on the `<link>` firing `load` or `error` (font-catalog.ts:189-191). The sibling caller in the same PR treats that as a real hazard and bounds it — `pdf-actions.ts:44-50` races the same promise against a 5s timeout precisely because "a stylesheet that neither loads nor errors (an offline tab, a CSP that swallows the request)" must not stall the flow. Here there is no bound, so in that case the canvas keeps painting the fallback with no corrective repaint, whereas the pre-change code at least repainted once. Partly masked by the editor's global `loadingdone` listener (packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:1063), which is why this is minor rather than major.

samples.summary: Theme font apply drops `ensureFontLink`'s promise and never asks the Font Loading API, so the theme family may never be fetched for canvas paint

Nothing in the slides frontend ever calls `document.fonts.load` for a theme family (grep: only apply-font-family.ts:40 and pdf-actions.ts:54), and canvas `fillText` does not trigger a lazy CSS face download, so the face only arrives if some DOM node happens to paint in it (the picker trigger's `style={{fontFamily: value}}` is the accidental trigger). finding.evidence: Both editors repaint *on font arrival only*: `packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:1063` listens for `document.fonts` `loadingdone` and calls `clearMeasureCache(); markDirty(); render()`, and `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2676` does the same. verdict.reason: Verified independently: `releasePreviewFontLinks()` (font-catalog.ts:246-253) and `removePreviewFontLink()` (:224-226) only call `link.remove()` — no event, no callback, no measure-cache clear. Both canvas consumers invalidate on font ARRIVAL only (slides/editor.ts:1062-1069 `loadingdone` → clearMeasureCache/markDirty/render; docs/editor.ts:2671-2692 `loadingdone` → clearMeasureCache/invalidateLayout/render, plus a mount-only `fonts.ready` fallback). Repo-wide greps found no head MutationObserver, no CustomEvent/dispatchEvent in text-formatting, and no other `loadingdone`/`fonts.ready` consumer that could catch a removal. Of the three release sites, only the pick path is followed by a repaint (apply-font-family.ts:35-46; docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:345-362 via editor.focus()); the Esc/outside-click dismiss path (font-family-picker.tsx:244-249 returns without applyPick, cleanup at :175-178; more-fonts-dialog.tsx:174-177) releases with no repaint and no cache clear, so a canvas that was already re-measured and repainted from the subset face (which `loadingdone` guarantees when the subset loads) keeps that paint and its poisoned (font,text)→width entries. Reachable because nothing preloads document-used families at open: `collectFontFamilies` is used only by pdf-actions.ts:43, and the other ensureFontLink callers are hover/pick/theme-builder — so a non-eager family the doc uses has no full link, `hasFullFamilyLink` (font-catalog.ts:352) does not suppress the subset, and a Recent row for that family is visible immediately on open. Stale render plus stale metric cache is an incorrect-state/broken-invariant bug in the Correctness lane, major impact.

verdict.reason: The unawaited `ensureFontLink(family)` at docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:350 exists as described, but the claimed harm — `FontRegistry.ensureFont` calling `document.fonts.check()/load()` in the pre-parse window and caching `status='loaded'` forever — is unreachable. The very next statement guards on `store.fonts?.ensureFont?.` (line 351-354), and nothing in this repository ever populates a `fonts` member on a DocStore: `DocStore` declares none (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:11-120), `MemDocStore` has none (grep for `fonts` in packages/docs/src/store returns no matches), and the frontend's `yorkie-doc-store.ts` has none. `FontRegistry` (packages/docs/src/view/fonts.ts:278-333) is exported at packages/docs/src/index.ts:188 but is only ever instantiated in packages/docs/test/view/fonts.test.ts:63 — never in production code. So the Font Loading API is never invoked after the unawaited call on any real path (apply at :359, prefetch at :449/:646), and no 'loaded' status is ever recorded. The toolbar comment at :342-344 and the plan doc at docs/tasks/archive/2026/05/20260529-docs-font-controls-plan.md:1507 confirm the registry wiring is deliberately absent/out of scope. Additionally, the docs canvas relayouts on `loadingdone`/`fonts.ready` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2668-2692), so no stale-metrics invariant is broken by the missing await. The dropped promise is a shape inconsistency with apply-font-family.ts:35 and pdf-actions.ts:48, not a behavioral defect under the correctness rubric.

finding.summary: A row scrolled past now leaves a glyph-subset @font-face connected for that family, so document text using the family renders half-real / half-fallback (previously scrolling loaded the whole family)
finding.evidence: `ensurePreviewFontLink` injects `css2?family=X:wght@N&text=<label glyphs>`. Google's `&text=` response has NO `unicode-range`, so the face applies to every codepoint of family X. Nothing else in the app loads a full link for a family merely present in the document: `useGoogleFontsLink()` (docs-view.tsx:213, slides-view.tsx:230) only requests `eager` families, and `ensureFontLink` is called only on apply/hover (apply-font-family.ts:28, theme-builder-panel.tsx:100, toolbar `onPrefetch`). So for a reloaded doc that uses a non-eager family, the pre-change behaviour was "scroll the picker → full family arrives → canvas repairs"; now scrolling injects only the label's glyphs, and the canvas/DOM paints those glyphs in the real face and every other character per-glyph fallback — mixed faces and inconsistent measurement, and the subset link is never removed unless a full link later loads (font-catalog.ts:197).

verdict.reason: The finding's load-bearing mechanism — "the subset link is never removed unless a full link later loads (font-catalog.ts:197)" — is not what the code does. `releasePreviewFontLinks()` (font-catalog.ts:246-253) removes EVERY `link[data-wafflebase-font-preview]` from the head, and both (and only) preview surfaces call it on the lifetime boundary of their list: FontFamilyPicker has a cleanup effect keyed on the portalled menu element (font-family-picker.tsx:175-178 — Radix unmounts DropdownMenuContent on close, so `setListEl(null)` fires the cleanup) and also calls it synchronously before handing a pick to `onChange` (font-family-picker.tsx:198, `applyPick`), and MoreFontsDialog does the same keyed on its scroll container (more-fonts-dialog.tsx:174-177). So a family whose row was merely scrolled past does NOT keep a subset face after the list closes; the document reverts to exactly its pre-open state. This is exercised by the repo's own test "closing the menu releases the row subsets" (font-family-picker.test.ts:445-464, asserting `previewLinks()` is empty after Esc). I enumerated every caller of `ensurePreviewFontLink` (font-family-picker.tsx:150, more-fonts-dialog.tsx:152 — the only two) and every caller of `releasePreviewFontLinks`; there is no preview-injecting path that lacks a release. Additionally, `ensurePreviewFontLink` refuses to inject a subset whenever ANY full css2 link for the family exists — including the app shell's own index.html link — via `hasFullFamilyLink` (font-catalog.ts:289-308, guard at :352), so a family the app actually loaded in full is never subsetted. What remains is only a transient, explicitly designed tradeoff: while the picker/dialog is open, a family the document uses but that nothing ever loaded in full (previously rendering entirely in fallback) may paint the previewed glyphs in the real face. That is cosmetic, self-healing on close, and reversible — not the persistent half-real/half-fallback document state the finding describes, and not a crash, data-loss, or broken-core-flow defect under the correctness rubric.
